# Decision catalog oracle

Read [the fixed104-object catalog](decision-catalog-baseline.json). It comes from `git show 4bb200fb7c2f9a8e1e929de0e2cbcab6c9151f0c:src/data/models.ts`, imported by Bun before feature009. Original serialized snapshot SHA256: `70d8e1865e3da60c153c99d18aa212e29c2879aa5a4949c345947cea07ef352e`; committed formatter-normalized fixture SHA256: `2a0a4581b7fffb5ff51112420011010973637952e4c428dae4d626ed4ec5fb9e`. The two parsed arrays were verified equal in every field and in order.

Read [the acceptance witness](../acceptance/decision-models-acceptance.py): it verifies fixture hash/count and projects the candidate catalog onto the104 historical IDs, then compares every pre-existing object and its relative order. Later new IDs are allowed; deletion, duplication, field changes or historical reordering fail. Luna uniqueness/category is checked separately. No Git history lookup, fetch, or temporary external file is required to load this baseline. The current CI checks out full history (`fetch-depth:0`), but the oracle also works in a shallow clone. This fixture supplies an independent baseline only; request/response behavior uses per-test factories.
